thread:
Tessa Morgan: dropping latest Figma for usage insights breakdown table + top cost drivers cards. would love quick eyes today — worried we’re drifting into “too much data at once”. https://figma.com/file/ri-usage-insights/breakdown-table-top-drivers?node-id=842-1190

Alicia Perez: thx. first impression: table is super dense. 9 columns + sparkline + row actions feels like a spreadsheet, not “insights”.

Alicia Perez: biggest concern: explainability. “Top drivers” shows % deltas but I don’t know what it’s *attributing* (token out vs cache miss vs retries). we need a sentence that answers “why is this high?”

Dylan Brooks: +1 on density. eng-wise we can support fewer columns and put the rest behind a “Columns” picker, but we should decide defaults.

Marissa Cole: agreed. goal is “find cost drivers fast”, not recreate billing export.

Nora Ahmed: table right now has: Route, Model, Cost, Requests, Tokens In, Tokens Out, Cache hit %, Retries, Avg latency. that’s… a lot.

Felix Schneider: from a data POV, retries + fallbacks are still squishy. showing them as first-class columns could create support pain when numbers look off.

Logan Wright: also note cache hit % is only meaningful if we define whether it’s prefix cache vs KV cache etc (we currently have “cache outcome” in events but it’s not perfect across all regions). showing it without context might mislead.

Alicia Perez: suggestion: default columns should be: Route, Model, Cost, Tokens Out, Cache (maybe as “Cache savings” not “hit %”), and “More” drawer for the rest.

Alicia Perez: “Requests” is important but maybe in drilldown instead of main table? depends on persona.

George Mbatha: from the research side: eng leads want cost per route/model + what changed since last week. finance wants export + totals match invoice. both groups get overwhelmed by low-level metrics unless there’s a narrative.

Alex Martinez: DX perspective: “route” vs “endpoint” terminology continues to trip people. in the UI we should label as “API endpoint” and tooltip the normalized route concept (templated paths).

Tessa Morgan: good call. i can swap label to “Endpoint (normalized)” + tooltip copy.

Marissa Cole: top drivers cards: can we make them more “insight-like”? e.g. “Token output increased +35% (wo/w) on /v1/chat/completions → llama-3.1-70b” with a “Why?” hover that lists the contributing factors.

Dylan Brooks: we can generate an explanation string from the heuristics service (ENG-3819). but we need to be careful it doesn’t sound overly confident.

Felix Schneider: exactly. language should be probabilistic. “Likely drivers” / “We observed” instead of “caused by”.

Alicia Perez: yes. also: card layout currently has 3 mini charts + a long list of bullets. clutter. pick one primary stat + 1 small trend, and make the rest expandable.

Tessa Morgan: so: collapse detail by default? “Show details” accordion under each driver?

Alicia Perez: i’d do: Card headline, 1-line explanation, then “View breakdown” link. Avoid multiple tiny visuals.

Nora Ahmed: on the table, can we avoid showing both Tokens In + Tokens Out at once? users mostly care about out in our pricing. input matters for context length distribution but that’s more drilldown.

Logan Wright: +1. plus we don’t have perfect context length histogram yet; we have p50/p95 context length as derived fields but they’re not in the aggregation for v1.

Marissa Cole: what about “Tokens” single column with subtext “in/out” on hover? or default “Tokens out” and drilldown shows in/out + context length distribution.

Alex Martinez: and please add tooltips for “Tokens out” vs “Output tokens billed” — users ask whether streaming changes token count. also retries/fallbacks create confusion.

Dylan Brooks: another note: row-level “% of total” could be huge for prioritization. that might replace some columns.

Alicia Perez: yes! “Cost” + “% of total spend” is a better scanning aid than requests/latency. keep the table about spend.

George Mbatha: in interviews, “latency” is only relevant once they’ve identified a cost hotspot. they’ll click in. having it in the main table reads as “this is equally important.”

Tessa Morgan: ok, propose default table columns:
- Endpoint
- Model
- Cost
- % of total
- Tokens out
- (optional) Cache savings
Everything else via “Customize columns” + drilldown.

Felix Schneider: love that. and put a “Data freshness” badge at top (not per-row) so we don’t add more noise.

Marissa Cole: re “cache savings” — do we actually have a $ savings estimate? if not, stick to “Cache hit rate” but with tooltip + show only in drilldown until we’re confident.

Logan Wright: we can compute “cached tokens” vs “uncached tokens” more reliably than a $ savings estimate in phase 1. savings requires pricing + assumptions.

Dylan Brooks: to reduce clutter: maybe show “Cache: 42%” but only when available; otherwise show “—” and tooltip “Not available for this deployment/mode yet”.

Alicia Perez: careful with lots of “—” rows. makes the table feel broken.

Nora Ahmed: we can hide columns with low availability by default. only show cache column when the filter is Hosted/Dedicated where coverage is good.

Marissa Cole: +1. the UI can conditionally recommend columns based on coverage.

Tessa Morgan: top driver cards — what’s the minimum to solve explainability?

Alicia Perez: each card needs:
1) What changed (metric + delta)
2) Where (endpoint + model)
3) Why we think so (1 sentence)
4) What to do next (link to docs/lever)
No more than that on the surface.

Alex Martinez: for “What to do next”, make it a small “Recommended next step” with 1 link (e.g. “Reduce output tokens” → docs on max_tokens/stop/structured output). Don’t list 6 recommendations.

Dylan Brooks: we can cap to one recommendation per driver. and add “See more recommendations” in drilldown.

Felix Schneider: also we should add a “Not all spend is attributable” disclaimer somewhere if we have untagged routes early beta. don’t want design to imply 100% coverage if it’s not.

Marissa Cole: agree. but keep it subtle; maybe an info callout under totals: “Some requests may be grouped under ‘Unknown endpoint’ until instrumentation fully rolls out.”

Tessa Morgan: noted. i’ll revise:
- simplify table defaults (cost-first)
- add % of total
- rename “Route” to “Endpoint” with tooltip about normalization
- top drivers cards: 1-line “likely driver” copy + progressive disclosure
- reduce visuals on cards

Alicia Perez: :thumbsup: can you also check spacing? current card grid feels cramped (too many elements above the fold).

Tessa Morgan: yep. will push an updated frame later today.

Marissa Cole: thanks all. once updated, we’ll do quick review w/ Dylan + DevEx to ensure copy matches what backend can support.

Dylan Brooks: sounds good. pls tag me when updated; we’re trying to keep parity with what query API can return in v1.

George Mbatha: if you want, i can share 2–3 verbatim quotes from interviews about “too many metrics” + “why is this high” to help with microcopy.

Tessa Morgan: yes please. drop here when you have them.

George Mbatha: will do.

Alex Martinez: also small ask: add tooltip for “Model” column to clarify alias/version bucketing (users will ask why they see “llama-3.1-70b” instead of “llama-3.1-70b-instruct-2025-12-xx”).

Tessa Morgan: good catch. adding to tooltip list.

Felix Schneider: (last) please avoid calling it “Top cost drivers” if it’s actually “Top spenders” in v1. driver implies causality. maybe “Top spend contributors” + “What changed” for deltas.

Marissa Cole: love that distinction. we can reserve “drivers” for when we’re confident in the heuristics.

Tessa Morgan: ok, rename in UI to “Top spend contributors” for beta, and “What changed” section for delta insights. done.

Alicia Perez: :white_check_mark: that should reduce support blowback too.

Dylan Brooks: +1. shipping something explainable beats shipping something “fancy”.
